Audio Priority Bar 2.13.0 mutes the speakers when your headphones disconnect, now by default, and mutes every microphone at once instead of only the one in use. It also holds the microphone when AirPods keep taking it back, lets a dock's output be used without its microphone, and lists recent switches in Settings. Coming from 2.12.0, the update installs in place, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Speakers

- **Mute speakers when headphones disconnect** is now on for anyone who never changed it, so headphones that run out of battery or turn off no longer leave the speakers playing at full volume. Turn it off in **Settings › Devices** ([#77](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/77)).

## Microphone mute

- Muting now covers every connected microphone, not only the one in use, so a call app or browser tab set to another microphone hears silence too. Virtual inputs are left alone, a microphone you had muted yourself stays muted, and unmuting, quitting or a crash restores each one ([#80](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/80)).
- A Bluetooth headset microphone that isn't the one in use stays live, since muting it could drop its sound to call quality. If an app records from it while you're muted, the reminder names both, for example "Google Chrome is using AirPods Pro, which isn't muted".

## AirPods

- When AirPods in your ears take the microphone back, the app now takes it back every time instead of giving up after the second try, so a call stays on your microphone. It only pauses, for 30 seconds, when another app takes it back within a second three times in a row ([#81](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/81)).

## Docks and audio interfaces

- A device with both an output and a microphone, such as a USB-C dock, has **Use Its Microphone Too** in its row's actions menu, on by default. Uncheck it to use the dock's output while your Microphones list picks the microphone ([#78](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/78)).

## Troubleshooting

- **Settings › App** lists the last 20 switches with the reason for each, and **Copy Diagnostics** copies them with your settings and device lists, ready to paste into a bug report ([#79](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/79)).
- **Keep a debug log**, in the same place and off by default, records device changes, switches and clicks in a file per day, the last 7 days kept ([#76](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/76)).

## Fixes

- A Jabra headset that dropped mid-call no longer shows a call that already ended when it comes back ([#73](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/73)).
- With **Volume level** on, an output without volume control, such as an HDMI display, no longer leaves an empty gap beside its icon in the menu bar. Thanks to Masaiki for this one ([#75](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/75)).

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is signed with the project's own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Connecting a Bluetooth device from the panel asks for Bluetooth permission, and Accessibility is optional, for the hover preview. Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
